title: SkillResolutionPacket
description: NON-AUTHORITATIVE. The full, deterministic record of which promoted skill versions were selected for one mission and — equally important — which were considered and refused, with reasons. This packet is not evidence: nothing reads it to route, to decide a check status, or to gate delivery. It exists so that a person can see what shaped the worker's proposal, including the skills that did not.

authoritative.description: Always false. Present so that no consumer can render a skill's advice as evidence by accident.

selected.description: Promoted versions injected into this mission's worker, in deterministic role order.

version_hash.description: Content hash over skill.json AND SKILL.md together, recomputed on load. A mismatch makes the version unavailable — it is never silently used.

evaluation_status.description: Read from the registry, never from the skill. A UI may only say 'verified' when this is PASSED; absent or failed renders as absent or failed, never as blank.

considered.description: EVERY version the resolver looked at, with its outcome and a machine-readable reason code. Carried in full because a rejection nobody can see is indistinguishable from a skill that was never there.

outcome.description: BLOCKED is a refusal on principle (lease excess, forbidden authority, integrity failure). NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION is a genuine conflict a machine must not resolve by guessing — it is never settled by prompt wording.

conflicts.description: Conflicts detected BEFORE the worker runs, so a mission never spends tokens on a SkillSet that was never coherent.

unavailable.description: Promoted versions that failed their integrity check. A promoted version whose content no longer hashes to its approved hash is a security event, not a missing file — reported here, never silently dropped.

needs_human_decision.description: True when at least one conflict must be resolved by a person. The resolver never breaks such a tie itself.

error.description: Set when resolution itself failed. A broken registry degrades to a recorded error and an empty SkillSet — a mission runs with no skills rather than with unverified ones.
